question: A complete hydatidiform mole has 46,XX karyotype derived entirely from paternal chromosomes (androgenetic diploid) and carries a higher risk of malignant transformation than a partial mole.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect — this statement is true. Complete moles are 46,XX, purely of paternal origin, and carry a 15–20% risk of progressing to GTN. Partial moles are triploid and have <5% malignant potential.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A complete mole is androgenetic diploid (46,XX, all paternal DNA), contains no fetal tissue, and has a 15–20% risk of developing into GTN. A partial mole is typically triploid (69,XXX or 69,XXY) and has <5% risk of malignant transformation.
